claims.text: UN Regulation No.156 requires manufacturers to implement a certified Software Update Management System (SUMS) and UN Regulation No.155 requires a Cyber Security Management System (CSMS); the EU delegated acts set transitional application dates for software-update/type-approval rules (new vehicle types from 7 July 2024 and all new vehicles from 7 July 2026).
claims.publisher: Council of the European Union (document C(2022) 3823 final)
claims.about: UN R155/R156; EU type-approval and software-update timelines

claims.text: The EU Data Act (Regulation (EU) 2023/2854) gives users of connected products the right to access and share the data generated by those products (including vehicles) and became applicable on 12 September 2025.
claims.about: EU Data Act — in-vehicle data access

claims.text: The EU Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) creates legally binding obligations for high‑risk AI systems embedded in products and sets a timeline of staged application and review milestones that extend through 2028–2031 (including transition and reporting deadlines listed up to 2 August 2031).
claims.about: EU AI Act — high‑risk AI requirements and timelines

claims.text: BMW already delivers Remote Software Upgrades (over‑the‑air updates) and a 'Functions on Demand' ConnectedDrive Store that lets customers buy or trial vehicle functions and install them over the air (example: BMW Remote Software Upgrade announced 11 October 2022).
claims.about: BMW Remote Software Upgrade; Functions on Demand; OTA features

claims.text: The BMW Group has selected AWS as preferred cloud provider for its next‑generation automated‑driving development platform for the Neue Klasse and describes that cloud+partner approach as enabling faster development and delivery of ADAS and OTA features for Neue Klasse vehicles.
claims.about: BMW — AWS partnership for Neue Klasse ADAS and cloud development

claims.text: Qualcomm and BMW jointly introduced the Snapdragon Ride Pilot automated‑driving solution in the BMW iX3 (a Neue Klasse production vehicle) and Qualcomm later announced a multi‑year role as BMW’s lead compute silicon provider, signalling BMW’s move to high‑performance, centralized compute and AI platforms that will underpin OTA‑delivered ADAS and in‑car services.
claims.about: Qualcomm‑BMW collaboration; Snapdragon Ride Pilot; centralized compute for Neue Klasse

claims.text: Industry and technology consultancies and vendors forecast that software‑defined vehicle architectures, expanded over‑the‑air updates and 'feature‑on‑demand' / subscription business models will scale across OEM lineups through the late 2020s and into 2030 (shifting significant vehicle value toward software and recurring revenue).
claims.about: SDV, OTA and feature‑on‑demand market trends

claims.text: Telematics and industry market research shows accelerating adoption of embedded infotainment platforms, Android Automotive / OEM app‑store deployments and in‑car app ecosystems among European OEMs—enabling larger app marketplaces and third‑party services in EU cars across the 2028–2031 horizon.
claims.about: Android Automotive / OEM app stores and in‑car app ecosystems (Europe)

claims.text: BMW has stated that the Neue Klasse will begin production in 2025 and that the BMW brand transition to the Neue Klasse technology and new retail model in Europe will start from 2026, which implies the OEM’s software‑first architecture and OTA/Functions‑on‑Demand approach will be rolled through more model segments in the late 2020s (affecting compact/premium models over 2028–2031).
claims.about: BMW Neue Klasse roll‑out timetable and portfolio transition
